findings.description: The MODIFIED requirement still carries the pre-change obligation: line 27 says that where the CLI refuses the request, socrates "SHALL record that the servers were loaded", and the scenario at line 47 says "the run records that the servers were loaded". The implementation does the opposite on exactly that path: with the empty allowlist in place no server loads, `recordToolServers` (internal/agent/claude.go:117) returns without recording anything, and the change's own tests assert zero such events for this scenario (internal/agent/claude_test.go:136 and internal/e2e/retry_test.go:85, both tagged `// scenario: A machine that will not let them be ignored`). Line 27 also contradicts line 24 of the same requirement ("SHALL record what that event reported"), so the requirement has two competing owners of what gets recorded, and the one that would be archived as the spec is the one the code refuses to satisfy.

The line a person now reads when servers did load is "the tool servers this machine configures were loaded, and the seal is what holds the reviewer read-only: ...". That is the reassurance this change exists to withdraw: the proposal states the fallback "was accepted on the belief that the seal answered it. It does not", and the spec delta itself says the seal "bounds the worktree rather than the machine". So on the one machine where the invariant has actually been lost, the log tells the reader the reviewer is held read-only, which is the claim the design calls false.

`rejectedBeforeOpening` fires on any first attempt that errored before an `init` event with no text and no structured output, so it covers far more than a refused flag: a missing binary (`TestAnAgentThatWasNeverThereFails`), a `--settings` an older CLI does not know, a non-JSON warning line printed before the stream (parseStream returns `notAnEvent` before `init`), a provider error at startup. Two consequences on those paths. First, the run's log states a cause nobody checked: `EventStrictnessRefused` renders as "the CLI would not ignore the machine's tool servers, so the review was asked again without that: starting claude-that-is-not-installed: ...". Second, the retry drops `--mcp-config {"mcpServers":{}}` and `--strict-mcp-config` for a reason unrelated to tool servers, so on any machine the second attempt reads the machine's MCP configuration files with only the allowlist left, including the machine the design names where the allowlist can be overridden by `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`. The breadth of the trigger is stated in the design; recording it as a strictness refusal, and dropping the flag on failures that had nothing to do with strictness, is not.

The `strict-tool-servers-refused` path always writes the canned `strictnessRefused` constant ("You cannot use --strict-mcp-config when an enterprise MCP config is present") and never `response.Stderr`, which `withDefaults` only fills for `non-zero-exit`. So `TestARewordedRefusalIsStillRetried` (internal/agent/claude_test.go:218), whose scenario sets `stderr: "a message socrates has never seen"`, is delivered the exact wording socrates used to match on. The test passes identically against the deleted `strings.Contains(err, "cannot use --strict-mcp-config")` code, so the guard tasks.md 3.3 claims ("reword the simulator's refusal and confirm the retry still happens") proves nothing. Fix: have the refusal path emit `response.Stderr` when it is set, falling back to the canned message.

This section now describes superseded behaviour and is contradicted by the change. Line 58 lists the invocation as `--mcp-config {"mcpServers":{}} --strict-mcp-config` with no mention of the `--settings '{"allowedMcpServers":[]}'` this change makes the primary mechanism; line 62 says "there is nothing socrates can do about it from inside the invocation", which the change disproves; line 63 says the refusal "records `agent-tool-servers-loaded`", which is now `agent-strictness-refused`. Previous changes to this property updated this file as a task (see the archived 2026-08-20 change, task 2.2), and this change has no documentation task at all.

"Where the CLI refuses to ignore the machine's own configuration, the review runs anyway and the run records that the servers were loaded, because the seal is what holds the reviewer read-only" - both halves are now wrong: the allowlist stops the servers so nothing records them as loaded, and the seal-based justification is the one the proposal retracts. README.md:140 carries the same sentence ("the run says so, because the seal holds the reviewer read-only whatever is loaded"). Neither file is touched by this change.

The `kinds` list this guard scans for enumerates every other event kind the core writes but omits `agent.EventStrictnessRefused`, so the invariant "only the renderer may turn an event kind into a line" is unenforced for the kind this change adds: a second file naming the literal "agent-strictness-refused" would not be reported. Add `agent.EventStrictnessRefused` to the list; internal/presentation/messages.go is already in `convention.EventKindsNamed`, so nothing else moves.

`wireToolServer.Status` is parsed and then discarded: every name in `mcp_servers` is recorded as loaded regardless of status. The recordings show the real CLI reports a status per server, so a server the CLI lists as failed or needing auth (one that contributed no tools) will still produce an `agent-tool-servers-loaded` event naming it. The direction is conservative and nothing branches on the event, so this only costs a misleading log line.

Task 7.5, the live run against a machine with a managed tool-server configuration, is the only check that the real CLI accepts `--settings` with inline JSON and honours `allowedMcpServers: []`, and it is unticked. Nothing in the suite can substitute: the simulator's `allowsNoToolServer` parses the same key socrates writes, so a key the real vendor ignores or has renamed reads as working everywhere in the tests. Worth knowing that the change's central mechanism is, by the author's own accounting, still unverified end to end.
`_ = simulated` is vestigial: `simulated` is already used at line 203, so the statement does nothing.

risk_rationale: The code change is bounded and additive and the new reading path is sound, but the spec delta that would be archived states the opposite of what the code and its own tests do, the retry trigger drops the flag on failures unrelated to tool servers, and one user-facing line plus three docs still assert the reasoning this change retracts.
